name: Watercress

schedule.notes: Surface-sow into a constantly-moist medium. Easier from rooted cuttings.
Fall is the better season — heat triggers bolting.
Snip top 3 to 4 in of each stem; regrows quickly.

harvest.cues: Stems 6+ in, leaves dark green and round, before flowering. Peppery bite peaks pre-flower.
harvest.storageNotes: Stems in a jar of water in the fridge 1 week. Best fresh.

varieties.name: Common Watercress
varieties.notes: The classic. Grows in streams and constantly-wet garden beds.

varieties.name: Upland Cress
varieties.notes: Different species, similar flavor, grows in normal garden soil. Easier for most home growers.

notes: Needs constantly running or replaced water for the true species — bog garden, kiddie pool with weekly refresh, or a flowing stream. WARNING: never harvest watercress from agricultural runoff or pasture streams; can carry liver flukes. Upland cress is the no-fuss alternative.
